rows.question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
rows.answer: You must have a minimum of **75% attendance** in each course (calculated separately for theory and practical components) to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination. This is explicitly stated in the rulebook, and failure to meet this requirement will prevent you from taking the exam unless the shortage is condoned under Regulation 4.3.

rows.question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
rows.answer: In a theory course, your total marks are split as follows: 40 marks for internal assessment (including mid-term tests and assignments) and 60 marks for the end-semester exam. This is explicitly stated in the regulations.

rows.question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
rows.answer: To pass a course, you must score at least **30% in the end-semester examination** and **40% of the total marks** (combining internal assessment and the end-semester exam). If you fail either requirement, you will receive a grade of 'F'.

rows.question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
rows.answer: You will receive the letter grade **A+ (Excellent)** for 85 marks, as the grading table specifies that 80 to 89 marks fall under this category.

rows.question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
rows.answer: You have **ten working days** from the declaration of results to apply for re-evaluation of your theory course marks. No applications will be accepted after this period.

rows.question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
rows.answer: If you miss an end-semester exam due to illness, you must submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the exam. Upon acceptance of the certificate, you will be allowed to take the exam in the next supplementary examination, and this attempt will count as your first attempt without needing to pay the supplementary exam fee.

rows.question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
rows.answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall, your examination in that course will be cancelled, and you will be awarded the grade **F** in that course. This is treated as a **first offence**, even if the phone is switched off. Repeated offences carry stricter penalties, including cancellation of all semester exams or expulsion.

rows.question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
rows.answer: The hostel gates close at **10:30 p.m. every day**. If you return after this time, you must sign the late-entry register and provide a reason for the delay.

rows.question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
rows.answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. The Hostel Handbook explicitly prohibits the use of induction cooktops along with other high-wattage electrical appliances. Violations will result in confiscation of the appliance and a fine of Rs. 1,000.

rows.question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
rows.answer: If you pay your semester fees after the due date but before the last date, you will be charged a late fee of **Rs. 100 per day**, up to a maximum of **Rs. 1,500** for the entire payment. This fee applies until the last date specified in [FS §2.1].

rows.question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
rows.answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee is **31 July 2026**. After this date, no payment is accepted, and a late fee applies. If you miss this deadline, you will be treated as not registered for the semester unless the Registrar approves your request within five working days after the last date.

rows.question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
rows.answer: You are eligible for the **Merit-cum-Means Scholarship** if your **annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000** and you meet the academic requirement: a **CGPA of at least 7.0** (for continuing students) or **80% marks in the qualifying exam** (for first-year students). You must also submit an income certificate issued by a Tehsildar or equivalent officer, not older than six months, with your application.

rows.question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
rows.answer: Yes, you are entitled to bereavement leave if there is a death in your immediate family. You will be granted up to seven days of leave, which will count as attendance, provided the death is of a parent, sibling, grandparent, or spouse. You must inform your Head of Department (HoD) via email or the student portal before or during the leave and submit a written application upon your return.

rows.question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
rows.answer: No, you will not receive your hall ticket if you have not paid your tuition fees by the last date. The rule explicitly states that a hall ticket will not be issued to students with outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment. Your hall ticket will be released only after clearing the dues and provided the examination has not yet commenced.

rows.question: How long can a break of study be?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address this situation. The closest clause covers a related case: You may be permitted a break of study for **one semester or one academic year** on medical grounds, certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean. This break cannot be granted more than once during your programme.

rows.question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
rows.answer: You must complete the B.Tech. programme within a **maximum period of seven academic years** from your date of first admission. The rule states, *'A student must complete all requirements of the programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission.'*

rows.question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not specify whether a mess rebate applies for an absence of two weeks. The only relevant passage addresses rebates for absences of seven days or more.

rows.question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
rows.answer: You are covered under the Institute’s group medical insurance scheme for hospitalisation expenses of **up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year**. The premium is already included in your development fee, so no additional cost applies to you.

rows.question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
rows.answer: The rulebook gives two conflicting rules for condoning attendance shortages below 65%. **AR §4.3** states that a shortage of attendance below 65% shall **not** be condoned under any circumstances, while **LM §2.2** allows condonation if the student's attendance is **not less than 55%** and the shortfall is due to certified illness. You must check with the Dean or HoD to resolve this discrepancy, as one of these cannot both be true.

rows.question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
rows.answer: The rulebook contains conflicting thresholds for condoning attendance shortfall on medical grounds. [LM §2.2] states that condonation is allowed if attendance is **not less than 55%**, while [AR §4.3] requires attendance to be **not less than 65%** for condonation. Both sections address the same situation but specify different minimum attendance percentages.

rows.question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
rows.answer: The rulebook gives two different answers for your refund if you withdraw before classes begin. [SF §6.2] says you get **100% of the tuition fee back minus a 10% processing charge**, while [FS §4.1] says you get **100% of the tuition fee back with no deduction**. Neither rule mentions the caution deposit refund in the same way, but both agree it is refunded in full.

rows.question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
rows.answer: The rulebook contains conflicting requirements for maintaining your Merit Scholarship. [AR §11.2] states you must maintain a CGPA of **not less than 7.5** at the end of each semester, while [SF §3.1] requires a CGPA of **not less than 8.0** for the same purpose. Both sections explicitly address the continuation of the Merit Scholarship based on CGPA thresholds.

rows.question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss the end-semester exam due to a family wedding. The closest passage covers only medical grounds for absence from exams.

rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can get a re-test for missing a mid-term test due to a job interview. The closest passage covers leave for placement interviews but does not mention re-tests for missed mid-term exams in such cases.

rows.question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not specify whether grace marks are given if you fail a course by one or two marks. The closest passage covers the passing requirements for a course, which require a minimum of 30% in the end-semester examination and 40% overall.

rows.question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not specify whether you may write your answers in Hindi instead of English for the end-semester exam. The closest passages cover passing requirements, examination schedules, and hostel vacating procedures.
